solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Proposed bathing lake for a paddle

parts.note: bade = proposed, offered (past of bid)
L = lake, as on maps

explanation.surface: Someone suggests a swim in the lake, and a paddle is on offer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Paddle' reads as a wade at the water's edge, but it is the flat part of an oar: a blade.
explanation.definitionFit: The blade is the flat end of an oar or paddle, and a paddle's blade can stand for the whole.

clue.text: One's wobbly and pale, scratching bottom with skin condition

definitions.note: 'One's wobbly' is a whole description, 'one that is wobbly', standing for the noun

parts.note: BLANCH (turn pale) without its last letter H
mange is a skin disease of animals

explanation.surface: A sickly patient, shaky and pallid, with an itchy rash they can't stop scratching.
explanation.walkthrough: Everything suggests an unwell person, but the wobbly one is a pudding: blancmange is a set, jiggly milk dessert.
explanation.definitionFit: A blancmange is a molded milk jelly famous for wobbling on the plate.

clue.text: Get clean fires with hard wood

indicators.note: to fire someone is to sack them

parts.note: to wash = to get clean
W = with, the abbreviation, which is removed

explanation.surface: Cleaning a stove that burns a hard wood.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fires' sits beside 'wood' as if the logs were burning, but it means dismisses, and what gets dismissed is W for 'with'.
explanation.definitionFit: Ash is a tough, springy hardwood used for tool handles and bats.

clue.text: Secretive matter requiring attention goes to auditor

parts.note: to give someone your ear is to pay attention

indicators.note: an auditor is a hearer, so the word is given as it is heard

parts.note: a whack is a go, an attempt, so goes = whacks

explanation.surface: A confidential matter that needs attention is passed to the auditor for checking.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Secretive' reads as hush-hush, but here it means secreted by the body. 'Auditor' is an accountant in the surface and simply a listener in the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Earwax is matter secreted by glands in the ear canal.

clue.text: Lawn game put away without a ball served

parts.note: croquet is played with mallets and hoops on a lawn
to put away food is to eat it: ATE, minus A

explanation.surface: A garden game is packed up because no ball has been served.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Served' makes the ball sound like one in tennis, but it is a ball of food brought to the table.
explanation.definitionFit: A croquette is a small crumbed ball or roll of mashed food, fried and served.

clue.text: Arrange to have medicine bottle returned if no good

indicators.note: to bottle is to enclose, so the medicine holds the next pieces inside it

parts.note: a cure is a remedy, a medicine

indicators.note: returned means sent back, so the two words are read in the opposite direction

explanation.surface: Instructions to have a bottle of medicine sent back if it turns out to be useless.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Medicine bottle' looks like one object, but 'bottle' is a verb: CURE holds ONFI ('if no' 'returned') and G.
explanation.definitionFit: To configure is to set up or lay out the parts of something in a particular way.

clue.text: Conclusion of two contrasting periods coming up

indicators.note: in a down entry, coming up means read from bottom to top

parts.note: an age is a very long period
a mo is a very short period, a moment

explanation.surface: Two opposite eras approach and one of them ends.
explanation.walkthrough: The contrast is length: an age lasts ages, a mo passes in a moment.
explanation.definitionFit: Omega is the last letter of the Greek alphabet, hence the end, as in 'alpha and omega'.

clue.text: Object after evacuation of floor in university block?

indicators.note: after means the object word comes after the rest
in means the emptied floor sits inside the university word
evacuating a word empties it, leaving only its outside letters

parts.note: outer letters of floor
an object is an end, an aim

explanation.surface: A cryptic note on an objection after a university floor is cleared.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Block' is a social-media sense, hence the question mark.
explanation.definitionFit: On social media, to remove someone from your contacts is akin to blocking them.

clue.text: Despot's end connected to incendiary bombing may be this

definitions.note: 'this' points back at the whole clue: a despot's end by bombing is a tyrannicide

indicators.note: the end of a word is its last letter

parts.note: last letter of despoT

indicators.note: bombing blows INCENDIARY apart into a new order

parts.note: anagram fodder

explanation.surface: A tyrant's death caused by a firebomb attack.
explanation.walkthrough: 'This' is the definition, and it refers to the wordplay itself: a despot's end brought about by bombing may indeed be a tyrannicide.
explanation.definitionFit: Read straight, the clue pictures a despot killed by a firebomb, which is exactly what tyrannicide names.

clue.text: Get married in city boasting fine cathedral of trees

parts.note: Ely is a small English city in the Fens with a famous cathedral
M = married

explanation.surface: A couple plan a wedding in a city known for its cathedral.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cathedral of trees' pretends to be an avenue of arching branches; the cathedral belongs to Ely and only 'of trees' defines.
explanation.definitionFit: Elmy means full of or relating to elm trees.

clue.text: Attachment on plugs from now on attached to plug

parts.note: a plug is an advertisement, an ad
hence = from now on
re = on, concerning

explanation.surface: An attachment fitted onto electrical plugs, joined to another plug from now on.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Plug' appears twice: the first is a verb meaning fill, the second a noun meaning an advert.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: to adhere is to stick, and the noun names that state of being attached.

clue.text: Student group gathering in university?

indicators.note: to gather in is to take into a fold

parts.note: a form is a school class
U = university

explanation.surface: A body of students meeting on campus.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue does both jobs: a forum is a meeting for discussion, like a student forum held at a university.
explanation.definitionFit: A forum is a meeting or place where people gather to discuss things.

clue.text: Company land grabs cultivating endless corruption

parts.note: Co = company
a land is a nation
TAMING (cultivating, as land is tamed) without G

explanation.surface: A corporate land grab dressed up as farming, riddled with graft.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Corruption' reads as bribery in the surface; the answer takes its other sense, spoiling or pollution.
explanation.definitionFit: Contamination is the corrupting of something pure by impurities.

clue.text: Retired engine parts assembled on a line employing imperial measures?

indicators.note: parts means splits apart, so the reversed engine is pushed into the middle of the assembled letters
assembled means put together, so the letters are built into a new order
retired means withdrawn, going backwards, so the word is reversed

parts.note: loco, short for locomotive, is a railway engine

explanation.surface: An old locomotive is taken apart and its parts put together on a production line in imperial units.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Imperial measures' suggests feet and inches; here it means the policies of empire. 'Parts' is a verb: the reversed engine splits the rearranged ON A LINE.
explanation.definitionFit: Neocolonial policy is a modern form of empire-building, extending power over other nations by economic or political control.

clue.text: Bank limits left earl with 500 on account

parts.note: to bank on is to rely on

indicators.note: the pieces are joined together

parts.note: port = left side of a ship
E = earl
D = 500 in Roman numerals

explanation.surface: A bank caps the funds an aristocrat can leave in his account.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bank', 'account' and '500' all point at money; 'on account' is the definition, meaning by others' accounts.
explanation.definitionFit: Reportedly means according to what people report, on their account.

clue.text: Wild curry leaves are reportedly arriving from the east

indicators.note: in an across answer, coming from the east means travelling right to left, so the letters are read backwards
leaves means goes away from, so that letter is taken out of the curry

parts.note: a korma is a mild, creamy curry

indicators.note: reportedly says the word is only heard, so are stands for the letter that sounds the same

parts.note: said aloud, are sounds like the letter R

explanation.surface: Curry leaves, an Indian ingredient, said to be coming in from the East.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Curry leaves' looks like the herb; 'leaves' is a verb. KORMA without R gives KOMA, then 'arriving from the east' turns it round.
explanation.definitionFit: To run amok is to behave wildly and out of control; the word comes from Malay.

clue.text: Made without stock, gravy can stretch

parts.note: jus is a thin gravy or meat juice
a tin is a can
a stretch is time served in prison

explanation.surface: A cook's note: gravy made without stock, from a can, to make it go further.
explanation.walkthrough: The kitchen surface makes 'stock' a broth; the definition means stock as inventory, as in manufacturing that holds no spare parts.
explanation.definitionFit: Just-in-time production makes goods as parts arrive, keeping no stock in reserve.

clue.text: Director checked material having spent time reflecting on it

indicators.note: having spent means having used up, so that letter is gone from the cloth

parts.note: tartan is the checked woollen cloth of Scottish clans

indicators.note: reflecting means mirrored, so the words on it are read backwards

explanation.surface: A film-maker checks some fabric and, having wasted time, thinks it over.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Checked' looks like a verb but describes the cloth. TARTAN loses one T to give TARAN; 'reflecting' ON IT gives TINO.
explanation.definitionFit: Quentin Tarantino is the American film-maker behind Pulp Fiction and Reservoir Dogs.

clue.text: Minister suppressing recording's nervy ending

parts.note: a rector is a parish priest, a minister
an EP is an extended-play record

explanation.surface: A clergyman hushes up a tape that ends on a tense note.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nervy ending' sounds like an anxious finale; it is a nerve ending, which is what a receptor is.
explanation.definitionFit: A receptor is a nerve ending or organ that picks up stimuli.

clue.text: Bloody yellow-jacketed bees buzzing around jams and fruit

indicators.note: jams means squeezes into, so the jacketed bees are wedged inside the bloody word

parts.note: bloody means gory

indicators.note: jacketed means wrapped, so the heraldic yellow goes round the bees

parts.note: OR is gold or yellow in heraldry

indicators.note: buzzing around suggests flying about in disorder, so the letters of bees are rearranged

parts.note: the letters of bees

explanation.surface: A gruesome picture of yellow-striped bees swarming over jars of jam and fruit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Jams' looks like preserves alongside fruit; it is a verb, wedges in.
explanation.definitionFit: A tart green berry from a thorny bush, often made into fool or jam.

clue.text: One of old rotating ball pens?

definitions.text: One of old rotating ball pens?

indicators.note: rotating means turned round, so the letters are read backwards
pens means encloses, so the ball word holds the numeral

parts.note: an orb is a ball
one is the Roman numeral I

explanation.surface: A description of an old-style pen that writes with a turning ball.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue both defines and builds the answer: a ballpoint writes with a rotating ball.
explanation.definitionFit: The trade name for the ballpoint, invented by László Bíró, whose tip is a tiny rolling ball.

clue.text: North African close to climbing secure borders

indicators.note: borders means surrounds on either side, so the reversed word wraps round the other piece
climbing in a down answer means going upwards, so the word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: to nail is to fasten down, secure
by means near, close to

explanation.surface: A man from North Africa near to a climb, making sure of the frontiers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Close to' looks like a last-letter signal; it is BY. NAIL 'climbing' gives LIAN, which 'borders' BY.
explanation.definitionFit: A Libyan is a person from Libya, the country on Africa's Mediterranean coast between Egypt and Tunisia.

clue.text: Wrestling confederation's ace is very cocksure

indicators.note: wrestling twists and contorts, so the letters are rearranged
is here means becomes, so one letter is swapped for another

parts.note: the letters of confederation
A is ace in card notation

explanation.surface: A wrestling federation's champion is extremely arrogant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ace' looks like a champion; it is the letter A, which becomes V before the shuffle.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words describe someone excessively sure of themselves, with arrogant self-belief.

clue.text: Harvard student keeping daughter secret

indicators.note: to keep something is to hold it

parts.note: a coed is a female student at a US college
D = daughter

explanation.surface: A college student keeps a secret about her daughter.
explanation.walkthrough: Harvard is there to mark the student as American: coed is a US word.
explanation.definitionFit: A coded message is written in code, so kept secret.

clue.text: Glaze's tangy ingredient?

indicators.note: the answer is an ingredient of the words, part of their make-up

parts.note: glaZE'S Tangy

explanation.surface: What gives a citrus glaze its sharp flavour?
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is the definition too: lemon or orange zest is what makes a glaze tangy.
explanation.definitionFit: Zest is grated citrus peel, used to give a glaze its tang.

clue.text: Charlie crashing Polish Fiat

parts.note: to polish writing is to edit it
Charlie is C in the phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A man called Charlie smashes up a Polish-made Fiat car.
explanation.walkthrough: Fiat looks like the car, and Polish like a nationality; they are a decree and a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: fiat, Latin for 'let it be done', is an order by decree.

clue.text: Girl, no stranger to lower scores, turned over answer papers

parts.note: ID = identity papers
A = answer
MYRIAD (scores, a great many) turned over

explanation.surface: A pupil used to poor marks flips her exam over and hands in her answer papers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lower scores' reads as worse marks, but a lower is a cow (it lows), and the girl knows cows well.
explanation.definitionFit: A dairymaid works with milking cows, so no stranger to lowers.

clue.text: Bow's hurt ability to throw

indicators.note: Bow is in London's East End, where the Cockney accent drops the letter H at the start of words

parts.note: harm means hurt, injury

explanation.surface: An archer's bow has been damaged.
explanation.walkthrough: Bow looks like the archer's weapon, but it is the East End district, and a Cockney says HARM without its H.
explanation.definitionFit: A player with a good arm, as in cricket or baseball, is one who can throw hard and accurately.

clue.text: Volunteers painting poorly-lit boards around station feature

parts.note: TA = Territorial Army, Britain's volunteer reserve

indicators.note: the result is turned round

parts.note: an oil is a painting
dark = poorly lit

explanation.surface: Volunteers decorating dim hoardings around a railway station.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Station' is a railway in the surface and a broadcaster in the definition. 'Boards' is a verb, taking on board.
explanation.definitionFit: Talk radio is a format of phone-ins and discussion that features on some radio stations.

clue.text: Local objector losing pounds in fast

indicators.note: to lose something is to be left without it

parts.note: nimbly = quickly, fast
L = pounds (libra), removed

explanation.surface: A local protester shedding weight while fasting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fast' reads as going without food; it is an adverb, quickly.
explanation.definitionFit: A NIMBY (Not In My Back Yard) objects to developments near their own home.
